# Fixture corpus: what the 0.4.0 baseline wrote

> Source-path/product labels were translated during the November 4, 2026
> identity migration. All recorded corpus data bytes remain the frozen original
> baseline. Reproduce that historical producer using its archived pre-migration
> generator/build instructions in an isolated working area, not this checkout's
> renamed binary or rewritten example paths.

`threads.db` and `sessions-rs/` here are the files the **baseline binary** left
in `~/.craftsman` after four scripted runs against a mock model. The baseline is
`craftsman 0.4.0` built from the git tag `baseline-0.4.0` (commit `0b77980`). Later
changes to the storage layout are checked against data that code really wrote,
so a database that was written by an old binary keeps opening.

The directory name `v0.4.0` is the crate version that binary reports. It is not
a release tag (the latest release is `v0.3.0`); `baseline-0.4.0` is the
reference point of `docs/craftsman-harness-plan.md`.

The tests are in `crates/craftsman-rs/src/fixture_corpus.rs`. They copy these files
to a temp dir, because opening a WAL-mode database creates `-wal` and `-shm`
files, and never touch the originals.

## Files

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `threads.db` | 73728 | `274cd8eb7e4ffcf4fdf0af2692c1f8c69d81e7457c575429c5b17d390f4b8312` |
| `sessions-rs/fixture-http-400.jsonl` | 415 | `3323c80af443dea3d1733700a355b58321755787d1be6e16b966086987f15601` |
| `sessions-rs/fixture-plain.jsonl` | 185 | `ff6d937f0a52188c5b5baa5524d9e8072e454364723432eb18e07c3fdce78945` |
| `sessions-rs/fixture-tools.jsonl` | 1253 | `ab25251260abdd796ffc542e0b925000c0dd4da7d161e7c3be3f57c976507004` |
| `sessions-rs/fixture-write-file.jsonl` | 845 | `cb81f0b0c77d0a71ad375ec9ba00db6e1ba39f6ce4e5dbad0ee509fc0b7e62d6` |

A test (`readme_lists_the_sha256_of_every_corpus_file`) compares this table with
the files, so the corpus changes only through a reviewed diff that also updates
the table. `.gitattributes` keeps the bytes exact on every checkout (no line
ending conversion, `*.db` is binary).

`threads.db` is in WAL mode at `PRAGMA user_version` 0: the baseline never
stamped a schema version. A test pins its whole `sqlite_master` against a
literal list, so a column, index or table that a different binary adds shows up.

## The four threads

| Thread | What the baseline did |
|---|---|
| `fixture-plain` | A two-message exchange. |
| `fixture-write-file` | `write_file` and `edit_file` in one round: the workspace checkpoint tables hold a created file and a modified file with its pre-image. |
| `fixture-http-400` | `read_file`, then the second model round failed with HTTP 400: the stored thread ends in a tool call with no result. |
| `fixture-tools` | One round of three tool calls: `write_todos` (the state carries todos), `read_file` of a missing file (a tool message with `is_error` true) and `write_file` under `/memories` (a `store_files` row). |

The generator replaced what depends on the machine and the clock: thread and
workspace-checkpoint ids, all timestamps (a synthetic clock: thread *n* was
created at 1760000000 + 3600 *n* and updated ten seconds later), the workspace
path (now `/workspace`, also inside the failed tool's error message) and the
`store_files.modified` time. Everything else is as the baseline wrote it.

## Regenerating: not with a newer binary

The point of the corpus is that **the 0.4.0 code wrote it**. Regenerate only when
the corpus itself has to change, never to make a test pass, and never with a
binary built from anything but `baseline-0.4.0`. The generator refuses a binary
that does not report `craftsman 0.4.0` or that stamps `PRAGMA user_version`.

From the repository root:

```sh
git worktree add /tmp/craftsman-baseline baseline-0.4.0
(cd /tmp/craftsman-baseline && cargo build --locked --no-default-features -p craftsman-rs --bin craftsman)
python3 -I -B scripts/gen-fixtures-v040.py --binary /tmp/craftsman-baseline/target/debug/craftsman
git worktree remove --force /tmp/craftsman-baseline
```

The script prints the table rows above for the new files. It writes into this
directory by default, replaces only `threads.db*` and `sessions-rs/`, and
refuses any other `--out` that holds files it did not write (`--force` overrides
that). On one machine repeated runs write the same bytes. Bytes 96 to 99 of
`threads.db` record the SQLite library of the Python that last wrote it (the
committed file: Python 3.15.0 with SQLite 3.53.1, `002e95c9`); another Python
changes those bytes and nothing else.

## Not here yet

- **The two sanitised real databases.** The plan (`docs/craftsman-harness-plan.md`,
  phase P0) asks for "a fixture corpus generated by running the tagged binary
  against the mock server plus two sanitised real databases". Only the
  mock-server corpus exists. The real databases need a real `~/.craftsman/threads.db`
  from a user, sanitised, and are still open.
- Shapes the mock-server corpus does not contain: `suspension_json` is NULL in
  every checkpoint (no interrupted turn waiting for approval), and no stored
  system message.
